newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish PTC cellphone firm plans $150 mln yankee.
newsitem.headline: Polish PTC cellphone firm plans $150 mln yankee.

text.p: Poland's Polska Telefonia Cyfrowa-ERA GSM digital cellular phone operator said on Thursday it planned to issue a yankee bond worth about $150 million in the third quarter of this year.

It said in a statement the bond issue would be managed by U.S. investment bank Salomon Brothers and that it also planned to take out a syndicated loan worth about $400 million, which would be arranged by Citibank.
"As a part of its long-term financing programme PTC plans to issue high-yield bonds on the U.S. market...The issue of the first tranche of PTC bonds is expected in the summer of 1997," PTC said.
"ERA GSM expects to raise about $150 million through the issue," it said.
PTC said interest on the bonds or other details of the planned issued were yet to be determined.
It said the issue would be the first of its kind set by a telecommunications firm from Central Europe.
PTC said the long-term financing plan also assumed taking out a long-term syndicated loan that would be arranged by Citibank.
"This will be one of th largest loans extended to a Polish company and its value is estimated at $400 million," it said.
But it added the details of the loan would not be announced until final agreements were signed.
PTC, one of Poland's two digital cellular phone operators, which markets its products under the ERA GSM brand, is an international consortium with a share capital of 471 million zlotys.

Its main shareholders are Polish industrial and trading conglomerate Elektrim SA with 32.5 percent of shares, U.S. cellular phone operator USWest with 22.5 percent and Deutsche Telekom cellular subsidiary DeTeMobil also with a 22.5 percent holding.
